lastText: File ClosedThe Coup That Didn't TakeContestedItalian High Command, 1939–1945End of hostilities: SEPTEMBER 1943: SPECULATIVE · filed with minor delayImmediate AftermathThis file closes on September 1943, a speculative branch's own ending rather than a date the documented record recognizes: six weeks of an Italian army fighting itself that the actual, bloodless ██████████ of July 1943 never had to spend. The human cost of this path runs higher than the ██████████ one at nearly every hinge point: Italy's own wartime dead, roughly 300,000 military and civilian combined split across two governments and a country fought over twice, were already among the higher tolls of any Axis power relative to population. A speculative path with almost no historical footing: the officer corps' actual loyalty to the constitutional monarchy in July 1943 proved ██████ than any loyalty to Mussolini personally. What this file records instead is a counterfactual crisis of legitimacy inside the regime's own institutions: one the losing war underneath it would have overtaken regardless of who ██████ the orders. A deliberate early withdrawal from the Alamein line concedes the same ground the ██████████ twelve-day battle eventually lost anyway, without first spending the attritional casualties a fuel-starved defense was never favored to hold.
